correctness.rationale: For the density printed in Lemma 4.1, the factor multiplying the power of \(z\) tends to a finite positive constant at zero, so \(\pi(z)\asymp z^{-2+2r/\sigma_{11}^2}\) there. The endpoint integral is finite exactly when \(-2+2r/\sigma_{11}^2>-1\), equivalently \(r>\sigma_{11}^2/2\). At equality the divergence is logarithmic and below it is a power divergence. At infinity the two algebraic exponents add exactly to \(-4\) and the exponential tends to one, so the tail is always integrable. Thus the displayed density is normalizable if and only if \(r>\sigma_{11}^2/2\). The source then defines its extinction threshold by integrating against that density, so the condition is required for the threshold and Theorem 4.2 as printed. A fresh exact check reproduced the exponent sum \(-4\), the critical exponent \(-1\), and the source example's safe inequality \(1/2>9/50\).
